adversarial_audit.objection: Uniformly sampling four partitions estimates the physical law.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It does not; equation (1) requires Plancherel source weights and multiplicity-biased final labels.

adversarial_audit.objection: A low sample mean is sufficient evidence of decay.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The report includes a support-size Hoeffding radius and forbids asymptotic inference.

adversarial_audit.objection: Mutual-information confidence also controls fractional moments.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Fractional moments have a larger multiplicity-dependent range and receive a separate radius.

adversarial_audit.objection: Classical compilation of the statistic demonstrates a quantum primitive.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It is a dephased diagnostic only and supplies no coherent associator or decoder.

claim_gate.reason: The finite estimator now targets the correct physical average, but its confidence and representation cost do not establish a growing-n theorem.

falsifiers_triggered: Uniform partition sampling is not the physical outer-label law.
A favorable maximal-dimension sector does not estimate the physical average.
Finite low means without confidence radii are not evidence of asymptotic delocalization.

proof_obligations.resolution: The triple tensor dimension identity normalizes every conditional final-label law through S6.
Outer tuples are sampled from the exact physical marginal before their coupling is compiled.
Finite S6 intervals and an exponential representation cost cannot prove an all-n rate.
Worst-case multiplicity makes the current fractional-moment Hoeffding radius broad.

summary: Replaced selected-sector Racah diagnostics by exact physical-law outer sampling with complete couplings.
